inline_text:
## Problem

The sync report said "in sync" on steps with work pending, and some of its counts were wrong. Reading the 2026-11-03 report showed:

- Invite read "in sync" with room additions pending. Directory and clean did the same.
- "No Slack account" counted each person once per room pass, so it was about double the real number.
- A person with two live Slack accounts could be invited under the second one to a room they were already in.
- Identity ran without name matches, so people on another address looked like they had no Slack account.
- CRM rows missing from the intake were described as probable test data.

## Fix

- `sync.py`: an exit 0 whose findings start with `apply with --write` or `re-run --write` reads DRIFT. Any other open finding reads the new `needs review`, which leaves the exit code alone. A run that wrote stays WROTE, and PARTIAL still wins.
- `invite_organizers.py`: counts people, with room additions as a separate tile. Anyone with two live accounts, or with reviewed rows that disagree, is held and not invited. Everyone held is named in the log and on the page. A column id that is no live account is treated as stale, and a deactivated lookup hit gives way to a live column id.
- `sync.py`: identity runs with `--suggest`. Suggestions are never written automatically.
- `sync_crm.py`: new wording for rows on the CRM but not the intake.

## Known limit

A person with no usable lookup hit whose reviewed rows disagree stays "no Slack account", with a warning in the log. They aren't invited, so it can't cause a wrong invite. Two different held people with the same name show as one in the held count and list; neither is invited.

## Verification

- New tests in `test_sync.py`, `test_invite_organizers.py` and `test_resolve_slack_ids.py`. The affected skill suites and the library tests pass with `gws` off the PATH, and pre-commit is clean.
- An independent review of the follow-up commits reproduced the invite and labelling defects fixed in the last two commits, and a re-check confirmed those fixes.
